stem: For simultaneous equations in variables \(x\) and \(y\), \(D_x = 49\), \(D_y = -63\), \(D = 7\), then what is the value of \(x\)?
solution:
**(A)** \(7\)
By Cramer's rule, \(x = \dfrac{D_x}{D}\).
\(\therefore x = \dfrac{49}{7} = 7\).
The value \(\dfrac{1}{7}\) is the ratio taken upside down (\(\dfrac{D}{D_x}\)), and \(-7\) carries the sign of \(D_y\), which belongs to \(y\), not \(x\).

stem: Which equation from the following is a quadratic equation?
solution:
**(B)** \(x(x + 5) = 2\)
A quadratic equation has the form \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\) with \(a \ne 0\), the highest power of the variable being 2.
\(x(x + 5) = 2 \Rightarrow x^2 + 5x - 2 = 0\), which is of degree 2.
\(\therefore\) it is a quadratic equation.
The equation \(\dfrac{5}{x} - 3 = x^2\) becomes \(x^3 + 3x - 5 = 0\) (degree 3), \(n - 1 = 2n\) is linear, and \(\dfrac{1}{x^2}(x + 2) = x\) becomes \(x^3 - x - 2 = 0\) (degree 3).

stem: The sequence \(-10, -6, -2, 2, \ldots\)
solution:
**(B)** is an A.P., Reason \(d = 4\)
\(t_2 - t_1 = -6 - (-10) = 4\), \(t_3 - t_2 = -2 - (-6) = 4\), \(t_4 - t_3 = 2 - (-2) = 4\).
The difference between consecutive terms is constant.
\(\therefore\) the sequence is an A.P. with \(d = 4\).
The value \(d = -4\) is \(t_1 - t_2\), the difference taken in the wrong order.

stem: Which number from the following cannot represent probability?
solution:
**(B)** 1.5
The probability of any event lies between 0 and 1: \(0 \le P(A) \le 1\).
\(1.5 > 1\), so it cannot be a probability.
The numbers \(\dfrac{2}{3}\), 15% (that is 0.15) and 0.7 all lie between 0 and 1.

stem: Find the value of the following determinant: \(\begin{vmatrix} 5 & -2 \\ -3 & 1 \end{vmatrix}\)
solution:
\(\begin{vmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{vmatrix} = ad - bc\).
\(\begin{vmatrix} 5 & -2 \\ -3 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = (5)(1) - (-2)(-3) = 5 - 6\)
\(\therefore\) the value of the determinant is \(-1\).

stem: Find the first term and common difference for the following A.P.: \(5, 1, -3, -7, \ldots\)
solution:
First term \(a = t_1 = 5\).
Common difference \(d = t_2 - t_1 = 1 - 5 = -4\). Check: \(t_3 - t_2 = -3 - 1 = -4\).
\(\therefore a = 5\) and \(d = -4\).

subtopic: Shares — Face Value, Market Value, Brokerage
stem: Face value of a share is Rs. 100 and premium is Rs. 65, then what is market value of that share?
solution:
When a share is at a premium, MV = FV + premium.
\(\therefore \text{MV} = 100 + 65 = 165\).
The market value of the share is Rs. 165.

\(S = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}\), so \(n(S) = 6\).

Complete the activity to determine the nature of roots of the quadratic equation \(m^2 + 2m + 9 = 0\).
solution:
\(m^2 + 2m + 9 = 0\)
Comparing with \(am^2 + bm + c = 0\): \(a = 1\), \(b = 2\), \(c = 9\).
\(b^2 - 4ac = 2^2 - 4 \times 1 \times 9 = 4 - 36\)
\(\therefore b^2 - 4ac = -32\)
\(\therefore b^2 - 4ac < 0\)
\(\therefore\) the roots of the quadratic equation are not real.

subtopic: Shares — Face Value, Market Value, Brokerage
stem: Smita has invested Rs. 12,000 and purchased shares of FV Rs. 10 at a premium of Rs. 2. Complete the activity to find the number of shares she purchased.
solution:
FV = Rs. 10, Premium = Rs. 2
\(\therefore \text{MV} = \text{FV} + \text{Premium} = 10 + 2 = \) Rs. 12
\(\therefore \text{Number of shares} = \dfrac{\text{Total investment}}{\text{MV}} = \dfrac{12000}{12} = 1000\)
Smita purchased 1000 shares. Check: \(1000 \times 12 = 12000\).

stem: Solve the following simultaneous equations: \(x + y = 5\); \(x - y = 3\)
solution:
\(x + y = 5\) ... (1)
\(x - y = 3\) ... (2)
Adding (1) and (2): \(2x = 8 \Rightarrow x = 4\).
Substituting \(x = 4\) in (1): \(4 + y = 5 \Rightarrow y = 1\).
\(\therefore x = 4\) and \(y = 1\).
Check: \(4 - 1 = 3\), which satisfies (2).

stem: Find \(k\) if \(x = 3\) is a root of quadratic equation \(kx^2 - 10x + 3 = 0\).
solution:
Since \(x = 3\) is a root, it satisfies the equation.
\(k(3)^2 - 10(3) + 3 = 0 \Rightarrow 9k - 30 + 3 = 0 \Rightarrow 9k - 27 = 0\)
\(\therefore 9k = 27 \Rightarrow k = 3\).
Check: \(3(9) - 30 + 3 = 27 - 27 = 0\).

stem: Find the 19th term of the following A.P.: 7, 13, 19, 25, ...
The taxable value of a wrist watch belt is Rs. 586. Rate of GST is 18%, then what is the price of the belt for the customer?
solution:
GST \(= 18\%\) of taxable value \(= \dfrac{18}{100} \times 586 = \dfrac{10548}{100} = 105.48\), i.e. Rs. 105.48.
Price for the customer = taxable value + GST.
\(\therefore\) price \(= 586 + 105.48 = 691.48\).
The price of the belt for the customer is Rs. 691.48. Check: \(586 \times 1.18 = 691.48\).

stem:
The annual investments of a family are shown in the following pie diagram. Answer the following questions based on it.
(a) If the investment in the shares is Rs. 2,000, find the total investment.
(b) How much amount is invested in the Post?
solution:
In the pie diagram, shares have a central angle of \(60^\circ\) and Post has \(30^\circ\). The whole circle of \(360^\circ\) stands for the total investment.
(a) Central angle \(= \dfrac{\text{investment in the item}}{\text{total investment}} \times 360^\circ\).
\(60 = \dfrac{2000}{\text{total}} \times 360\)
\(\therefore\) total investment \(= \dfrac{2000 \times 360}{60} = 12000\), i.e. Rs. 12,000.
(b) Investment in the Post \(= \dfrac{30}{360} \times 12000 = 1000\), i.e. Rs. 1,000.
Check: the angle for Post is half that for shares, and Rs. 1,000 is half of Rs. 2,000.

subtopic: Shares — Face Value, Market Value, Brokerage
stem: A share is sold for the market value of Rs. 1,000. Brokerage is paid at the rate of 0.1%. Complete the activity to find the amount received after sale.
solution:
Brokerage = MV \(\times\) rate of brokerage
\(= 1000 \times \dfrac{0.1}{100}\)
\(= 10 \times 0.1\)
\(= 1\), i.e. Rs. 1
Amount received after sale = MV \(-\) brokerage
\(= 1000 - 1\)
\(\therefore\) amount received after sale \(=\) Rs. 999.

stem: The numbers 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 are on the surface of one die. If this die is rolled once, then complete the activity to find the probability of getting a number on the upper face which is a perfect square.
solution:
\(S = \{2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12\}\)
\(n(S) = 6\)
Condition for event B: getting a perfect square on the upper surface of that die. Of these numbers only \(4 = 2^2\) is a perfect square.
\(\therefore B = \{4\}\), \(\therefore n(B) = 1\)
\(P(B) = \dfrac{n(B)}{n(S)} = \dfrac{1}{6}\)
\(\therefore P(B) = \dfrac{1}{6}\).

subtopic: Solving by Formula and Completing the Square
stem: Solve the following quadratic equation by formula method: \(y^2 + \dfrac{1}{3}y = 2\)
solution:
Multiplying both sides by 3: \(3y^2 + y = 6 \Rightarrow 3y^2 + y - 6 = 0\).
Comparing with \(ay^2 + by + c = 0\): \(a = 3\), \(b = 1\), \(c = -6\).
\(b^2 - 4ac = 1^2 - 4(3)(-6) = 1 + 72 = 73\)
\(y = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} = \dfrac{-1 \pm \sqrt{73}}{2 \times 3}\)
\(\therefore y = \dfrac{-1 + \sqrt{73}}{6}\) or \(y = \dfrac{-1 - \sqrt{73}}{6}\).
Check: the sum of the roots is \(\dfrac{-2}{6} = -\dfrac{1}{3} = -\dfrac{b}{a}\).

subtopic: Mean, Median and Mode of Grouped Data
stem:
In the following table, the toll (in Rs.) paid from 6 am to 6 pm by drivers and the number of vehicles is shown. Find the mean of the toll by 'assumed mean' method.

| Toll (Rs.) | No. of Vehicles |
|---|---|
| 300–400 | 80 |
| 400–500 | 110 |
| 500–600 | 120 |
| 600–700 | 70 |
| 700–800 | 40 |
solution:
Take the assumed mean \(A = 550\) and \(d_i = x_i - A\), where \(x_i\) is the class mark.

| Class | Class mark \(x_i\) | \(d_i = x_i - 550\) | Frequency \(f_i\) | \(f_i d_i\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 300–400 | 350 | \(-200\) | 80 | \(-16000\) |
| 400–500 | 450 | \(-100\) | 110 | \(-11000\) |
| 500–600 | 550 | 0 | 120 | 0 |
| 600–700 | 650 | 100 | 70 | 7000 |
| 700–800 | 750 | 200 | 40 | 8000 |
| Total | | | \(\sum f_i = 420\) | \(\sum f_i d_i = -12000\) |

\(\bar{d} = \dfrac{\sum f_i d_i}{\sum f_i} = \dfrac{-12000}{420} = -28.57\) (approximately)
\(\bar{x} = A + \bar{d} = 550 - 28.57\)
\(\therefore \bar{x} = 521.43\) (approximately)
The mean toll is Rs. 521.43 (approximately). Check: it lies in the class 500–600, which holds the largest frequency.

stem: Manisha wants to distribute 540 bananas among some students. If 30 students were more, each would get 3 bananas less. Find the number of students.
solution:
Let the number of students be \(x\). Each student gets \(\dfrac{540}{x}\) bananas.
With \(x + 30\) students, each would get \(\dfrac{540}{x + 30}\) bananas.
\(\dfrac{540}{x} - \dfrac{540}{x + 30} = 3\)
\(540(x + 30) - 540x = 3x(x + 30)\)
\(16200 = 3x^2 + 90x\)
\(x^2 + 30x - 5400 = 0\)
\(x^2 + 90x - 60x - 5400 = 0 \Rightarrow x(x + 90) - 60(x + 90) = 0 \Rightarrow (x + 90)(x - 60) = 0\)
\(x = -90\) or \(x = 60\). The number of students cannot be negative.
\(\therefore x = 60\).
The number of students is 60. Check: \(\dfrac{540}{60} = 9\), \(\dfrac{540}{90} = 6\), and \(9 - 6 = 3\).

stem: ₹ 2,000 is invested at 10 percent simple interest. Check at the end of every year whether the interest amount is in A.P. or not. If this is an A.P., then find the interest amount after 10 years.
solution:
Simple interest for one year \(= \dfrac{P \times R \times N}{100} = \dfrac{2000 \times 10 \times 1}{100} = 200\).
Interest at the end of the 1st year = Rs. 200
Interest at the end of the 2nd year \(= \dfrac{2000 \times 10 \times 2}{100} = \) Rs. 400
Interest at the end of the 3rd year \(= \dfrac{2000 \times 10 \times 3}{100} = \) Rs. 600
The sequence 200, 400, 600, ... has a constant difference \(400 - 200 = 600 - 400 = 200\), so it is an A.P. with \(a = 200\) and \(d = 200\).
\(t_{10} = a + (10 - 1)d = 200 + 9 \times 200 = 200 + 1800\)
\(\therefore t_{10} = 2000\).
The interest amount after 10 years is Rs. 2,000. Check: \(\dfrac{2000 \times 10 \times 10}{100} = 2000\).

subtopic: Mean, Median and Mode of Grouped Data
stem:
In one group of students; 10% students got 0 to 20 marks; 20% students got 20 to 40 marks; 35% students got 40 to 60 marks; 20% students got 60 to 80 marks and remaining 30 students got 80 to 100 marks, then:
(a) Prepare a grouped frequency distribution table.
(b) Find the mode of the marks scored.
solution:
The given percentages total \(10 + 20 + 35 + 20 = 85\%\), so the remaining 30 students form \(15\%\) of the group.
Total number of students \(= \dfrac{30 \times 100}{15} = 200\).
(a)

| Marks | Number of students |
|---|---|
| 0–20 | \(10\%\) of 200 = 20 |
| 20–40 | \(20\%\) of 200 = 40 |
| 40–60 | \(35\%\) of 200 = 70 |
| 60–80 | \(20\%\) of 200 = 40 |
| 80–100 | 30 |
| Total | 200 |

(b) The highest frequency is 70, so the modal class is 40–60.
\(L = 40\), \(f_1 = 70\), \(f_0 = 40\), \(f_2 = 40\), \(h = 20\).
\(\text{Mode} = L + \left[\dfrac{f_1 - f_0}{2f_1 - f_0 - f_2}\right] \times h = 40 + \left[\dfrac{70 - 40}{140 - 40 - 40}\right] \times 20 = 40 + \dfrac{30}{60} \times 20 = 40 + 10\)
\(\therefore\) Mode \(= 50\).
The mode of the marks scored is 50 marks. Check: it lies inside the modal class 40–60.

stem: Using information given in the following figure, find the length and breadth of this rectangle in cm.
solution:
Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal.
Top = bottom: \(5m + n = 2m + 3n + 5 \Rightarrow 3m - 2n = 5\) ... (1)
Left = right: \(m + n - 3 = 3m - 2n + 7 \Rightarrow -2m + 3n = 10 \Rightarrow 2m - 3n = -10\) ... (2)
Multiply (1) by 3: \(9m - 6n = 15\) ... (3)
Multiply (2) by 2: \(4m - 6n = -20\) ... (4)
Subtract (4) from (3): \(5m = 35 \Rightarrow m = 7\).
Put \(m = 7\) in (1): \(21 - 2n = 5 \Rightarrow 2n = 16 \Rightarrow n = 8\).
Length \(= 5m + n = 35 + 8 = 43\) (check: \(2m + 3n + 5 = 14 + 24 + 5 = 43\)).
Breadth \(= m + n - 3 = 7 + 8 - 3 = 12\) (check: \(3m - 2n + 7 = 21 - 16 + 7 = 12\)).
\(\therefore\) the length of the rectangle is 43 cm and the breadth is 12 cm.
figureNote: Rectangle with right-angle marks at all four corners; side labels: top 5m + n, bottom 2m + 3n + 5, left m + n - 3, right 3m - 2n + 7; p-10
